correctness.rationale: PASS: The shortest proper border of any word is unbordered and nonoverlapping; refining any longer chosen outer border forces lower maximum width, so greedily removing shortest borders is optimal. For binary period doubling p(i)=v2(i+1) mod2, the reflection p(n−1−a)=v2(a) mod2 for n=4^m classifies each remaining boundary group into either two mirrored single-symbol borders or one mirrored two-symbol border, ending in center 10. Counting even v2(j) produces L_{2m}=(2·4^m+1)/3. For odd exponent the injective uniform morphism maps borders to doubled borders and excludes odd lengths because intermediate centers end in 0. Thus L_{2m+1}=L_{2m}. Independently optimized all outer-border options by dynamic programming for k≤8; universal result rests on valuation proof.
